title: Not for the Pious Dead We Weep
description: Not for the Pious Dead We Weep in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Anna Laetitia Barbauld wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 568 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Mourner's Thoughts of Heaven”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Not for the pi-ous dead we weep; Their sor-rows now are o'er; The sea is calm, the tem-pest past, On that e-ter-nal shore.

lines: Not for the pious dead we weep;
The sea is calm, the tempest past,
O, might some dream of visioned bliss,
Where, on the bosom of their God,
Thence may their pure devotion's flame
To us their strong aspiring hopes,
Let these our shadowy path illume,
To welcome all that's left of good,

licence: Public domain: Anna Laetitia Barbauld died in 1825.
credits: Words by Anna Laetitia Barbauld (1743–1825), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
